A rectangular carton is 30 cm × 20 cm × 10 cm. How many 1-litre cartons of milk can fill it exactly?
questions.explanation: V = 30×20×10 = 6,000 cm³ = 6,000 mL = 6 L. So exactly 6 one-litre cartons.

questions.question: Volume of water in a pond is 500 m³. 1 m³ = 1,000 L. How many litres is that?
questions.explanation: 500 m³ × 1,000 = 500,000 L. Large volumes (ponds, pools, reservoirs) are measured in m³; 1 m³ = 1,000 L.

options: Both have equal volume (120 cm³ each)
questions.explanation: Box 1: 6×5×4=120 cm³. Box 2: 5×6×4=120 cm³. Same dimensions, different order — multiplication is commutative. Equal volumes.

A box of juice (18 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm) costs ₹30. Another box (12 cm × 8 cm × 4 cm) costs ₹25. Which is the better deal (more juice per rupee)?
questions.explanation: Box 1: V=432 cm³, cost ₹30 → 14.4 cm³/₹. Box 2: V=384 cm³, cost ₹25 → 15.36 cm³/₹. Box 2 gives more juice per rupee — better deal.

questions.question: A cylindrical drum has capacity 500 L. If it is ⅖ full, how many more litres are needed to fill it?
questions.explanation: ⅖ × 500 = 200 L already in drum. Remaining = 500 − 200 = 300 L needed.
